quote: A worker gives the platform four of its 64 physical cores, eight of its 128 logical processors, and little memory.
problem: 64 physical and 128 logical describe epn228; one of the three farm workers has 192 logical processors, so the sentence over-generalises a hardware count that Table 2 and Section 3.1 then repeat.
fix: Write: "A worker gives the platform four physical cores, eight logical processors of the 128 an EPN of the reference generation has, and little memory."

quote: A worker holds five log families, and InfoLogger is one of them (Table~\ref{tab:sources}).
problem: Table 1 has six rows, because it also lists the run orchestrator log that nothing collects, so a reader counting the table gets six, not five.
fix: Write: "A worker holds five log families, and InfoLogger is one of them. Table 1 adds the run orchestrator's log, which nothing collects."

problem: The section drops straight into a subsection, so the claim that the constraints made the design is never stated; Section 4 opens the same way.
fix: Add one sentence under the heading: "The constraints made the design, so they come first: what a node writes, how much of it, and what the farm will not give up."

quote: We kept its collector on every node, widened from two sources to five.
problem: Seven sentences in the paragraph open with We kept, We kept, We changed, We replaced, We dropped, We dropped, We dropped, which reads as a template.
fix: Merge the two kept sentences and the three dropped ones so the paragraph varies its subject.

quote: Collecting the run orchestrator's log is a deployment decision not taken.
problem: The phrase drops "that was", and the sentence sits between two unrelated facts with no connection to either.

quote: A storage quorum of two of three, and a lost worker loses only its own local index
